reason: Automated, inside ODD, approved and verified software. Stationary hazard 40 m ahead at 13.4 m/s: a careful driver stops with 5.3 m to spare even reacting in 1.5 s. The system first detected it 3.0 s after a human could have. Full sensor set, decision log, CCTV, police and 2 witnesses: clear recovery case.

Manual mode at the crash with human control inputs: an ordinary motor claim against the human driver. A careful driver would have stopped (5.3 m margin), but the human was driving, so there is no AEVA s.5 recovery from the tech company.

The system issued a transition demand 20 s before the crash and the user-in-charge never responded. Their immunity ends after a transition demand (AV Act 2024), and 20 s is ample time. Avoidable by a careful driver who took over, so the human is liable.

Transition demand only 3 s before the crash, too short for a human to take over and act. The hazard was avoidable for a careful driver reacting at once (5.3 m margin), and the system detected it 3.0 s late. Strong evidence.

Hazard appeared 10 m ahead at 13.4 m/s: even a fast careful driver (1.0 s) hits it, with a stopping shortfall of about 18 m. The system detected it 2.2 s BEFORE a human could have. No driving fault by the system, so there is nothing to recover.

28 m gap at 13.4 m/s: a fast careful driver stops with 0.1 m to spare, a slow one hits. Too close to call on a kinematic replay. Needs the full logs and a proper reconstruction before any recovery decision.

Self-driving engaged OUTSIDE its operating design domain. The tech side (operator or ASDE) carries the driving fault, and the crash was avoidable for a careful driver. Pull logs first to settle who let it run outside the ODD, operator or manufacturer: that decides the recovery target.

Tamper flag set and the CCTV clock is 1.8 s off the vehicle log. Until a human clears the evidence, neither the replay nor the detection timing can be trusted, so no liability call and no recovery decision.

Human control input within the last 3 s while automated: the human overrode the system just before impact. Human liable, subject to checking whether the override was a reasonable reaction to the system's behaviour.

A critical LIDAR_FRONT_DEGRADED fault was logged before the crash while automated: points to a product defect. The crash was avoidable for a careful driver (5.3 m margin). The fault log is direct evidence for recovery from the manufacturer.

The vehicle was running a software version not on the approved list, with no sign the insured altered it (no s.4 flags). The tech side ran unapproved software, and the crash was avoidable for a careful driver.
The insured made an unauthorised software change (AEVA s.4). The insurer recovers from its own insured under the policy (s.4(4)), not from the manufacturer, so the AV company is not the target.

Person in charge let the car drive itself when inappropriate (AEVA s.3(2)). Reviewer did not confirm that this puts liability on the human rather than the tech side, so it goes to review: pull the logs and take advice on how s.3(2) interacts with the recovery before deciding.

Lead vehicle braked at 4.4 m/s^2 from 11.4 m/s with a 16 m gap, dry road: a careful driver stops with 3.1 m to spare even at 1.5 s. The system detected it 2.5 s late. Inside ODD, verified engagement, full evidence. A small (£5,270) but clean claim, worth pursuing pre-issue.

Wet road (mu 0.4), 29.7 m/s, lead vehicle braking at 6.8 m/s^2 with a 29 m gap: harder than the following car can brake on that surface, so even a fast careful driver collides (61 m shortfall). Unavoidable for a competent human: no system driving fault.
17 m/s with a 23 m gap, lead braking at 5.7 m/s^2: a fast careful driver stops (8 m margin), a slow one hits by 0.6 m. Borderline: needs the logs and a better reconstruction.

Cut-in 43.5 m ahead, closing at 3.3 m/s: a careful driver keeps a 37 m margin. The system detected it 2.0 s late and still collided. Serious injury (£498,140 paid), inside ODD, decision log, CCTV, police report: strong, high-value recovery.

Clearly avoidable for a careful driver (13.5 m margin at 1.5 s) and the system detected the hazard 1.5 s late, so the driving fault sits with the system. But ODD status is unknown and there is no CCTV: pull logs to confirm it was operating inside its ODD before pursuing a £290,180 serious claim.

Fatal cut-in at 28 m/s, closing at 11.9 m/s from 28.5 m: a fast careful driver avoids it (5 m margin), a slow one hits by 1 m. Too close to call, and fatal: pull logs and reconstruct properly before any decision.

13.1 m/s, 13.2 m gap, lead braking at 6.5 m/s^2 on a dry road: a fast careful driver hits by only about 0.6 m and the system detected the hazard 2.2 s late. Reviewer did not accept 'no fault' on a margin this thin: unsure, so review and pull the logs.
